title: Bluff
text: “Is that so? Our motto is to offer our products at fair prices. Yes.”
“I don’t know about that…”

That’s Father’s skill right there. He knows of cheaper places at other shops. He’s bluffing, implying that this shop is expensive in comparison. His remark about there being a lot of Demi-Humans here also subtly conveys that he’s seen places where humans are sold. Just as I’d expect from Father.
“Still, I’m surprised that the Hero is interested in slaves. Yes.”
“As the Shield Hero, there’s no way I’m going to find allies in this country, right? I intend to make use of whatever I can.”
After swallowing hard, my Father answered bravely.
“You can’t become strong unless you use them with the intention of wearing them out.”
When he said that, the monster merchant’s face began to glow. This wasn’t some kind of visual effect—it really looked like he was excited, didn’t it?

“Depending on the situation, I might ask my ally, the Spear Hero, for help… but if there’s anyone you want eliminated, just say the word. I’ll take care of them cheaply. In return, sell me your slaves at a discount.”
“Understood. As for this Motoyasu, if it’s my Father’s wish, I’ll gladly assassinate a business rival.”
“Huhuhuhu… When I first saw you, you didn’t seem like a very good customer, but I suppose you can’t judge a book by its cover. Yes. I’ll reconsider my opinion. Yes.”

The monster merchant was in a great mood… He’s never shown me this kind of attitude before. I seem to recall him always looking perplexed—or did I? As expected of my Father—he really shines when it comes to negotiations.
“So? What kind of slave are you looking for? If you have a budget, I’d be happy to help you figure it out. Yes.”
My Father whispered softly into my ear.
“What should we do? I’m not entirely sure, but should we buy a slave based on the merchant’s recommendation? Or should we pick one ourselves?”

Hmm… That’s true. For the role of a salesperson, a slave with a friendly demeanor would be best. There’s no point in buying a slave who’s unfriendly for no good reason. It’d be wise to use my knowledge of the future here. If we buy a slave who handled peddling in Father’s village, we can avoid taking any strange risks.

So, who should it be? Let’s recall the slaves who performed well during the peddling trips organized by Filolial-sama and her group. Basically, under Father’s guidance, they should have all achieved a certain level of performance, but among them, there was one who stood out as particularly capable… If I recall correctly… I think a puppy that turns into a pig named Keel was one of the high-performing slaves.
“Well then—”

I’ll answer this in a whisper, so Father won’t hear. If I remember correctly, Keel—just like Big Sister—was a Demi-Human who lived in a village within the territory Father is set to develop. Something about how they were reduced to slavery due to the effects of the waves. I’ve heard this from Filolial-sama and the other slaves.
“Is there a slave here named Keel? They should be from a village destroyed by the waves.”
At Father’s words, the Monster Merchant pulled out a list and began scanning it. A little while later…
“Unfortunately, there isn’t one. Yes.”
Huh? I’d heard that Father generally acquired slaves through this monster merchant’s mediation—could that not be the case? Does this mean, just like with Filo-tan, the timing doesn’t match up?
“If you’d like, shall I search among my colleagues and have one brought in? Yes.”
Father crossed his arms and thought it over.
“You’re just going to charge a premium and provide a fake, aren’t you? That won’t fly.”

“What! Our reputation is our greatest asset. Yes. If we look among those who’ve recently become slaves since the wave hit Melromarc, I’m sure we can find one. Yes. Of course, the price will go up depending on the purchase price, but what do you say?”
“Then, silver coins…”
After checking the money in his pouch, Father replied.

“Up to fifty. I have no intention of paying a single coin more than that. It doesn’t have to be that particular one, mind you… Well, if you try to add anything extra at checkout… you know what’ll happen, right?”
“I’m thrilled by the Hero’s skill in haggling to the very end. Yes.”

My Father stares intently at the monster merchant as he clicks away, calculating the gold. When it comes to money, Father truly has a remarkable talent. If we ever end up in a loop, I’ll make sure to steer things in a direction where he can fully showcase this talent.
“Then please visit us again tomorrow. By then, we should know how long it will take to get the item.”
“Got it. See ya.”
With a light pat on my shoulder, Father left the tent. A little while later, I found myself standing in a corner of the back alley, my hand over my mouth.

“I’m hungry, but I can’t stop feeling nauseous… Even though they’re Demi-Humans, this is a place where humans are bought and sold… I’ve seen it in fiction, but the real thing has such a grim atmosphere.”
“Are you okay?”
“Yeah. I’m fine, but… ugh… I don’t think I’ll have an appetite for a while.”
Yuki-chan and the others were also terrified by the atmosphere inside the Monster Merchant’s tent, after all. It’s true that it’s not exactly a pleasant place.
“If things go well, we might be able to meet that girl, Keel, tomorrow.”
“That’s right.”
“Next… what should we do?”
“If you’re not feeling well, maybe we should rest?”
“I’m fine. If I get flustered over something like this, I don’t think I’ll be able to survive what lies ahead.”
What a wonderful mindset. I feel like I’ve caught a glimpse of my Father’s inner strength.
“Well, from now on, we’ll have to hide the fact that we’re getting stronger as much as possible. That being the case, I wonder if we can level up? I think it’ll be pretty difficult.”
“That won’t be a problem.”
I’ll keep talking to my Father in a whisper. You never know where someone might be eavesdropping on our conversation.
“First off, I think the best way to raise your level, Father, is to have Yuki-chan and the others help you.”
“I suppose so, but…”
“It’ll be fine. Shaking off pursuers and surveillance is a piece of cake if we use portals and teleportation Skills.”

“That’s true. Escaping itself is probably easy. I don’t know for sure, but when we went to Siltvelt, we were running from pursuers, after all. But in this case, isn’t the problem that we’ll suddenly vanish and show up with powerful allies? It’s also important to let the surveillance run its course to some extent. We need to make them draw the wrong conclusions.”

My father-in-law seemed to be thinking it over. You’re right—I hadn’t thought that far ahead. I’d been so focused on becoming strong enough to protect my Father from assassination. But if I get stronger too quickly, that’ll only lead to more persecution and aggressive interference against him, won’t it? I see—so the reason there were more assassins in the previous world compared to the first one was because we were strong.
“How about this? Motoyasu-kun could just act like nothing’s happened, simply because he helped me—”
My father offered a suggestion. I see—with that approach, we could certainly throw the watchers off the scent.

“So, I’ll head down to the town to see if I can make some money… I’ll sneak a peek at the herbs used for potions at the apothecary, then head out toward the grasslands. The monsters there are weak, so I think even I’ll be fine.”
“Understood. Then let’s get moving.”
“Yeah… Yuki-chan and the others, do your best, too.”
Yuki-chan and Kou chirped cheerfully from my shoulder.
“Thank you for everything so far, Motoyasu-kun! I’ll be fine on my own from now on, so go ahead and save the country!”
My Father spoke in a deliberately loud voice and gave me a pat on the back. I waved back at him in response.
“Well then, goodbye! If fate brings us together again, we’ll meet again!”

That’s right—people get suspicious because my Father and I are together. So we decided that, in the end, it would minimize the damage if we went our separate ways until we met up again. Of course, there’s a certain amount of risk involved, but Father told me to let him know if we ended up in a loop.
Well, whether it turns out for the best or the worst—I was anxious, but we went our separate ways, leaving Father behind.
